threads.body: `Scope` opened in `onEnter()` is only closed on normal returns because `@Advice.OnMethodExit` does not specify `onThrowable = Throwable.class`. If `TaskQueue.execute(...)` throws, the root-context scope will remain current and can leak context into subsequent work on the same thread. Add `onThrowable = Throwable.class` to the `OnMethodExit` (as done in other scope-closing advices) to ensure the scope is always closed.
The comment has a grammatical error: “executes a runnable that start consuming tasks” → “starts consuming tasks”.

`ContextPropagatingRunnable.propagateContext(...)` is intended to be used only for lambda runnables (see `ContextPropagatingRunnable.shouldDecorateRunnable` comment) because wrapping arbitrary `Runnable` instances changes their concrete type/identity and can break downstream logic that expects a specific implementation. Consider following the existing executor-instrumentation pattern: first check `ExecutorAdviceHelper.shouldPropagateContext(currentContext, task)`; then only wrap when `ContextPropagatingRunnable.shouldDecorateRunnable(task)` is true, otherwise attach the context via a `VirtualField<Runnable, PropagatedContext>` using `ExecutorAdviceHelper.attachContextToTask(...)` so the runnable instance is preserved.

New instrumentation is added for `io.vertx.core.impl.TaskQueue.execute(Runnable)` but there is no corresponding regression test covering the intended context-propagation behavior (and preventing propagation into the queue consumer runnable). Since the vertx-http-client 3.0/4.0/5.0 modules already have `VertxHttpClientTest` suites, consider adding a focused test case that exercises `TaskQueue` usage under concurrency and asserts the correct parent context/span is observed.
